chapter: Club Alabam and the Europe contract
title: Gus Schultz's rule against four-beat music on Saturday
summary: The maitre d' forbids sensuous four-beat playing on Saturday nights, and the club draws rich scions that prepared him for Europe.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, alright, let's go back to the stay at the Alabam now. You have a larger orchestra now.
And you're still writing arrangements, I guess, and, are the people dancing now to your, are they still listening --

Oh yes we had to play that, and that's one thing I wanted to tell you. In the Club Alabam, you could play any dancing you want until Saturday. But Saturday, Mr. Gus Schultz was the manager -- he was really the maitre d' of the club. He wouldn't stand for no four beats. You know, like, (plays piano). know why? Because he said it was sensuous music. And that would start women to twirlin' and movin', you see. And guys huggin' them close like that. You could play it more like, (sings), "Toot toot tootsie, goodbye", and stuff like that. On Saturday night, never. He taught me that. He'd raise his hand and say, "No, no." Don't go into nothing with four beats. Nothing beating out four times.
Because, see, New York didn't understand the blues. And those that understood it were in -- in high type places, they

wouldn't stand it. I know, one time, Gus come to me standing on the bandstand, and he said, "Sam, you see one of those steps over there?" He said, "There's five billion dollars represented on that. Scions from the different rich families." The guys are sitting on the steps, lounging on the steps, (unintelligible) Well, they're all from the Vanderbilts and the Astors, and the different rich families, they was just sitting there and laughing, and you'd think they were just a bunch of tramps. Something like that. Well that's the kind of people we had coming in there.
We had terrific people coming in there, see. And one thing it set us up for when we was to go to Europe, later on. We know how to entertain that type of people.
